newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares edge lower in early bourse trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares edge lower in early bourse trade.

text.p: German shares opened bourse trade weaker on Wednesday as the profit-taking that has followed recent record highs continued.
Dealers also said the market was on hold before U.S. September consumer price data due later in the day, which could contain some indications about the future direction of U.S. interest rates.
The DAX index of Germany's 30 leading shares fell 14.26 points, or 0.52 percent, to 2,714.19 in early trade, retreating from the record high of 2,728.64 reached briefly on Tuesday.
"We could be ready for a bit of a pause at the moment. But even if it goes down one percent, it's not really serious," one trader said.
The dollar, which had made gains against the mark in early European trade, slipped back to its Tuesday levels of around 1.5410 to the German currency.

The consensus forecast for U.S. September consumer price data, due at 1230 GMT, is for a rise of around 0.3 percentage points. But dealers said they were not expecting market reaction to the figures to be large either way.

Among individual shares, car-maker Volkswagen AG rose 6.75 marks to 590.50 as dealers said it benefitted from positive sentiment surrounding the sector after U.S.-based General Motors' rise in third-quarter profits announced on Tuesday.
Industrial group Mannesmann AG fell four marks to 582 in early bourse trade after it said it was halving tariffs on its D2 mobile phone network.
